slot.brief: Multi-step: identify dissociation (van 't Hoff factor) of a given electrolyte/complex, then compute osmotic pressure or boiling point elevation; combine formulas for a numeric answer.

stem: Assuming complete dissociation, what is the boiling-point elevation of a $0.20\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$ solution of $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ in water? Take $K_b=0.52\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Complete dissociation gives 3 ions per formula unit, so ΔT_b = iK_bm = 3(0.52)(0.20) = 0.312 K.

working:
$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2\to[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$.\n$i=3$.\n$\Delta T_b=iK_bm=3(0.52)(0.20)=0.312\ \text{K}$.

Independent check: Complete dissociation gives 3 ions per formula unit, so ΔT_b = iK_bm = 3(0.52)(0.20) = 0.312 K.
solution:
On complete dissociation, $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ produces $3$ ions, so $i=3$.
$$\Delta T_b=iK_bm=3(0.52)(0.20)=0.312\ \text{K}$$
